en: This collection of the *uccodarki*, the *nityābhinihata*, the *kṣepa*, and the *pūrvodātta* is made for the sake of perfecting the placement of the hands and the pronunciation [of these accents]. 1.
Since the definition of *saṃhitā* does not apply when a word has an acute accent (*udātta*) preceded by another acute accent within a single word, understand this accordingly.
The two types of acute accents— the *pracaya* and the ordinary— are distinct due to the difference in their position and the location of the voice.
In this [section], in the *goṣṭha*, *rāṣṭra*, *loka*, and *kṣaya* [chapters], as well as in the subsequent [chapter],
when the word *ni* ends in a long vowel and is not preceded by a *saṃbuddhi* [vocative], the *vṛtta* that occurs before *etadoḥ* is [as follows];
in the other two [chapters], however, for the word *vasuḥ*, the preceding syllable is *svarita*-accented.
From this world and from the intermediate space, what is the covering of food?
O Agni, go forth; that vessel of the inner self exists over there.
Having approached this very earth, the waters were held by the heat of Agni.
Bring us hither as steeds for our own sake; may he now beautify the praise-worthy food.
Having brought the fierce ones into the midst, let all be well-pleased; indeed, I now offer this with *svāhā*, for I am the one who overcomes them.
"Of this one, here, the thunderbolt of the waters rises up and comes down.
"For Indra, O inspired one, you are the impetuous one"—thus [he says]. There are three fire-pan (ukhā) verses. 8.
They should be for him the lords of the nameless ones; for the born and the unborn do not exist apart from the rain.
From our two eyes, or from us, the breath eats strength, O Aśvins.

Following light and food, [it goes] into Agni; for Bṛhaspati, the *traiṣṭubha* [verses], the *jayas*, the *iṅgyas*, and the *aṃśapadas* are elevated; the syllable following the *svarita* is [the *udātta*]. 10.
Having bowed to all the gods and my teachers, I shall now set forth this concise commentary (*laghuvṛtti*), which is a compendium of the *anudātta* [accent] following the *svarita*,
as proclaimed by Yamu; it consists of ten verses with an elevated conclusion for the sake of achieving proficiency in grammar for beginners.
Salutations to those whose tongues serve as the inner sanctum for the lotus feet of the venerable Keśavāryācārya— those who are jewels among the wise.
Thus ends the *Uccodarka*, composed by the venerable Keśavācārya.
